claims.text: vLLM v0.14.0 enabled async scheduling by default and added numerous engine, tool-calling, API, and model-support changes; the release notes explicitly call this a breaking change with unsupported configurations documented.
vLLM v0.15.0 added a Kimi-K2.5 architecture among new model support and extended async scheduling to pipeline parallelism, alongside streaming-input, quantization, and platform changes.
Any speedup figures in the release notes are project-reported and configuration dependent.

limitations.text: The series spans two releases nine days apart and should be summarized as serving/runtime evolution rather than one atomic feature.
Project performance claims are not independently reproduced.
